reason: Two oxlint defects explain 2 of the 3 reports: x.slice(-1)[0] in an initializer is reported twice (once from the member-expression path and once from the call-expression path, commander), and it is never reported on the right-hand side of an assignment because the skip for assignment targets fires for any AssignmentExpression parent (yargs-parser key = arg.slice(-1)[0]); the third is LAG (unicorn ignores DOM-like .children receivers).
evidence: Repro: const a = arr.slice(-1)[0]; -> oxlint 2 identical diagnostics, ESLint 1; let k; k = arr.slice(-1)[0]; -> ESLint 1, oxlint 0. prefer_at.rs check_slice_index_access returns false when parent_kind is AssignmentExpression(_) regardless of side. unicorn v66 #3102 'Ignore DOM collection receivers'. No oxc tracker hit.

reason: oxlint collects only the leading run of import declarations and stops at the first other statement, so imports after a statement such as TypeScript's hoisted var _a, _b, _c; are never checked (yargs-parser); ESLint checks every import declaration.
evidence: Repro: var _a; import { format } from 'util'; import { normalize, resolve } from 'path'; -> ESLint 'Expected multiple syntax before single syntax', oxlint nothing (same imports without the var: both report). sort_imports.rs run_once: for statement in program.body { if ImportDeclaration push else break }.

reason: For var bindings declared outside the loop oxlint counts only writes inside the loop, while ESLint treats any write after the loop start as unsafe, so a closure created in a loop that reads a var assigned after the loop (tslib __esDecorate's done = true) is missed.
evidence: Repro: var done = false; for (...) { out.push(function () { if (done) throw 0 }) } done = true; -> ESLint 'unsafe references to variable(s) done', oxlint nothing. no_loop_func.rs is_var_unsafe_in_loop only checks loop_span.contains(write); its let path uses ESLint's border logic. No oxc tracker hit.

reason: For one five-level ternary chain both tools report once, unicorn at the first ternary that is too deep and oxlint at the deepest one, four lines apart (entities escape.js 10 vs 14).
evidence: Repro: a five-level c === n ? ... : chain -> ESLint one report at the third ternary (line 6), oxlint one report at the fifth (line 10).

reason: oxlint returns early when the outer if is itself an else-if, so the final else { if (...) {} } of an if / else if / else chain is never reported (ajv parseJson, ws extension); ESLint reports it.
evidence: Repro: if (a) {} else if (d) {} else { if (b) {} } -> ESLint 'Unexpected if as the only statement in an else block', oxlint nothing (without the else-if both report). no_lonely_if.rs: if let AstKind::IfStatement(_) = parent_kind { return; }. No oxc tracker hit.

reason: Both reports are .some(x => x === value) predicates, which unicorn reports since v66; oxlint's port does not.
evidence: unicorn v66.0.0 release note 'prefer-includes: Simplify boolean array predicates (#3096)'; records: ajv allPs.some((p) => p === it.jtdDiscriminator), picomatch branches.some(branch => branch === '').

reason: Same finding on ignore's multi-line arrow function: ESLint reports at the => head and oxlint at the opening parenthesis of the parameters, three lines apart.
Same finding on the same multi-line arrow function as max-statements: ESLint reports at the => head, oxlint at the start of the parameter list, three lines apart.
evidence: Repro (max 1): ESLint 4:7, oxlint line 1; ignore index.js 1077 vs 1080, both 'too many lines (58)'.

reason: Both reports are in ignore's setupWindows, which turns the rule off with /* eslint no-control-regex: "off" */; ESLint (inline config on) obeys, oxlint does not read rule-configuration comments.
evidence: oxlint docs, Inline ignore comments: 'Comments must start with one of the keywords below' (disable/enable directives only) and 'Rule options cannot be changed inline'; oxc #12648 (open) lists /* eslint rule: "off" */ comments as unsupported.

reason: One promise chain, import(...).then(...).catch(...), is reported once by each tool: oxlint at the start of the chain and ESLint at the final .catch, five lines apart (lru-cache diagnostics-channel).
evidence: Repro: import('x')\n .then(...)\n .catch(() => {}) -> ESLint line 6 (catch), oxlint line 2 (import).

reason: oxlint skips any unused catch parameter whose name starts with an underscore, while unicorn (and oxlint's own docs) exempt only an unused _, so catch (_err) {} is reported by ESLint only (yargs).
evidence: Repro: try { y() } catch (_err) {} -> ESLint 'The catch parameter _err should be named error', oxlint nothing; catch (_) {} silent in both. catch_error_name.rs: if name.starts_with('_') && no references { return }; unicorn: originalName === '_' && no references (same in v60). oxlint doc: '`_` is allowed if it's not used'.

reason: The 2 oxlint-only reports are the typeof global / typeof self existence checks in tslib's root detection, which unicorn stopped flagging in v66; the guarded uses are reported by both.
evidence: unicorn v66.0.0 release note 'prefer-global-this: Don't flag typeof existence checks (#3070)'. Repro: typeof global === 'object' ? global : ... -> ESLint 2 reports, oxlint 4.

reason: oxlint treats an unscoped rule name with two slashes (eslint-plugin-node's node/prefer-global/process, has-flag) as invalid and reports the directive as naming no rules.
evidence: oxc #27364 (open) 'unicorn/no-abusive-eslint-disable reports directives naming rules with more than one slash', fix PR #27677 (open). Repro: // eslint-disable-line node/prefer-global/process -> oxlint reports, ESLint not.

reason: oxlint ignores this used in a parameter default, so ajv's errorsText(errors = this.errors, ...) is reported as a method that does not use this; ESLint counts the default value as part of the method.
evidence: Repro: class A { t(errors = this.errors) { return errors } } -> oxlint 'Expected method t to have this', ESLint nothing. No oxc tracker hit.

reason: oxlint skips every function whose parent is an object property, so qs's RFC3986: function (value) { return String(value) } (and shorthand methods) are never reported, while unicorn has reported both forms since at least v60; the oxlint test file keeps these unicorn cases commented out under a TODO, but there is no tracker issue.
evidence: Repro: ({ p: function (v) { return String(v) }, m(v) { return String(v) } }) -> ESLint 2 reports, oxlint 0 (arrow properties are reported by both). prefer_native_coercion_functions.rs returns when parent_kind is ObjectProperty; its tests: '// TODO: Get these passing.' above the commented-out object cases.

reason: oxlint reports args.length used as the fallback value in const length = _length || args.length (yargs), which unicorn reported until v63 and stopped flagging in v64 for value-producing || expressions.
evidence: unicorn v64.0.0 'explicit-length-check: Fix || fallback false positives (#2889)': 'It no longer warns for code like foo.length || bar() when that expression is used to produce a value'; v63 source reports any .length under a LogicalExpression. Repro: const n = a || args.length -> oxlint only.

reason: oxlint counts only params.items, which excludes the rest parameter, so (str1, str2, count, ...args) => {} has 4 parameters for ESLint and 3 for oxlint (yargs browser shim).
evidence: Repro: { __n: (a, b, c, ...rest) => 0 } -> ESLint 'too many parameters (4). Maximum allowed is 3', oxlint nothing. max_params.rs uses function.params.items.len() for functions and arrows. No oxc tracker hit.

reason: The file disables eslint-plugin-n's rule with // eslint-disable-next-line n/no-process-exit, and oxlint's directive matching ignores the plugin prefix, so it also silences unicorn/no-process-exit (yargs esm shim).
evidence: oxc #26115 (open) 'rule prefix is ignored in oxlint-disable directives'. Repro: the same process.exit(code) with and without the n/ directive -> ESLint reports both, oxlint only the one without.

reason: 737 of the 782 Biome-only reports are TypeScript's parenthesized indirect calls (0, fn)(), which ESLint's default allowInParentheses: true accepts; Biome documents parenthesized sequences as invalid and has no such option (it is still listed as 'Same as no-sequences').
evidence: biome explain noCommaOperator, Invalid example: 'const foo = (doSomething(), 0);'; ESLint no-sequences allowInParentheses defaults to true; migrating {allowInParentheses: true} yields plain "noCommaOperator": "error".

reason: biome migrate eslint turns max-params (ESLint default max 3) into "useMaxParams": "error" without a max, and Biome's default is 4, so all 267 four-parameter functions stop being reported; even an explicit ["error", {"max": 3}] loses its max in the migration (same pattern as BI-2's eqeqeq ignoreNull).
evidence: biome explain useMaxParams: 'max: The maximum number of parameters allowed (default: 4)'. Repro: .eslintrc {"max-params": ["error", {"max": 3}]} -> biome migrate eslint writes "useMaxParams": "error"; function f(a, b, c, d) {} -> ESLint reports, migrated Biome not.

reason: Most ESLint-only reports are names starting with _ (_i, _, _default) and unused imports, which Biome's noUnusedVariables exempts by design, or unused parameters (pkg, res, name), which Biome checks in its separate noUnusedFunctionParameters rule; the migrator maps no-unused-vars to noUnusedVariables only.
evidence: biome explain noUnusedVariables: 'There is an exception to this rule: variables that start with underscore' and 'This rule won't report unused imports ... enable noUnusedImports'; noUnusedFunctionParameters: 'Disallow unused function parameters'. Repro: function f(x, y) { return x } -> ESLint reports y, noUnusedVariables not.

reason: The 110 Biome-only reports are Infinity, NaN and parseInt(x, 10), which unicorn no longer flags by default (checkInfinity off since <=v60, checkNaN off and base-10 parseInt exempt by v70), while Biome keeps the older behaviour; the 39 ESLint-only reports are isNaN/isFinite, which Biome excludes on purpose (DOC).
evidence: unicorn 78 defaultOptions checkInfinity: false, checkNaN: false and isBase10OrNoRadixParseIntCall (v60 had checkNaN: true, no parseInt exemption); biome explain useNumberNamespace: 'The rule doesn't report the globals isFinite and isNaN because they have a slightly different behavior'.
